items.label: Show Input Settings
items.info: Show configuration options for all input devices: analog response, Multitaps, light guns, etc. Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

sections.label: System
sections.info: Configure base hardware parameters: region, BIOS selection, memory cards, etc.

items.label: Region
items.info: Specify which region the system is from. 'NTSC' is 60 Hz while 'PAL' is 50 Hz. 'Auto' will detect the region of the currently loaded content. Games may run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

items.label: BIOS Selection
items.info: Specify which BIOS to use. 'Auto' will attempt to load a real bios file from the frontend 'system' directory, falling back to high level emulation if unavailable. 'HLE' forces high level BIOS emulation. It is recommended to use an official bios file for better compatibility.

items.label: Show BIOS Boot Logo
items.info: When using an official BIOS file, specify whether to show the PlayStation logo upon starting or resetting content. Also enables the display of BIOS file name in OSD. Warning: Enabling the boot logo may reduce game compatibility.

items.label: Second Memory Card (Shared)
items.info: Emulate a second memory card in slot 2. This will be shared by all games.

items.label: CD read-ahead
items.info: Reads the specified amount of sectors ahead of time to try to avoid later stalls. 333000 will try to read the complete disk (requires an additional 750MB of RAM).

items.label: Dynamic Recompiler
items.info: Dynamically recompile PSX CPU instructions to native instructions. Much faster than using an interpreter, but may be less accurate on some platforms.

items.label: DynaRec threading
items.info: Run the dynarec on another thread.

items.label: PSX CPU Clock Speed (%)
items.info: Overclock or under-clock the PSX CPU. Should be much less than 100 (something like 57) due to some real hardware slowdowns not being emulated. Usually should be left at 'Auto', else glitches or hangs are likely.

items.label: Dithering Pattern
items.info: Enable emulation of the dithering technique used by the PSX to smooth out color banding artifacts. "Force" enables it even if the game turns it off. Increases performance requirements.

items.label: Threaded Rendering
items.info: When enabled, runs GPU commands in a secondary thread.

items.label: Frameskip
items.info: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Auto (Threshold)' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting. 'Fixed Interval' utilises the 'Frameskip Interval' setting.

items.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
items.info: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Auto (Threshold)', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

items.label: Frameskip Interval
items.info: Specify the maximum number of frames that can be skipped before a new frame is rendered.

items.label: Display Internal FPS
items.info: Show the internal frame rate at which the emulated PlayStation system is rendering content. Note: Requires on-screen notifications to be enabled in the libretro frontend.

items.label: Use fractional frame rate
items.info: Instead of the exact 50 or 60 (maximum) fps for PAL/NTSC the real console runs closer to something like 49.75 and 59.81fps (varies slightly between hw versions). PCSX-ReARMed uses the former "round" framerates to better match modern displays, however that may cause audio/video desync in games like DDR and Spyro 2 (intro). With this option you can try to use fractional framerates.

items.label: RGB32 output
items.info: Improves color depth for true color modes (most FMVs and occasional title screens). Causes higher CPU usage due to double memory bandwidth requirement, even in 15bpp modes. Takes effect on game reload only (libretro limitation).

items.label: Hi-Res Downscaling
items.info: When enabled, games that run in high resolution video modes (480i, 512i) will be downscaled to 320x240 by skipping lines and/or columns. May be useful on some devices with native 240p display resolutions that lack efficient hardware scaling.

items.label: (GPU) Slow linked list processing
items.info: Slower but more accurate GPU linked list processing. Needed by only a few games like Vampire Hunter D. Should be autodetected in most cases.

items.label: (GPU) Horizontal overscan
items.info: The PSX can display graphics way into the horizontal borders, even if most screens would crop it. This option tries to display all such graphics. Note that this may result in unusual resolutions that your device might not handle well. The 'Hack' option is intended for the widescreen hacks.

items.label: (GPU) Screen centering
items.info: The PSX has a feature allowing it to shift the image position on screen. Some (mostly PAL) games used this feature in a strange way making the image miscentered and causing uneven borders to appear. With 'Auto' the emulator tries to correct this miscentering automatically. 'Game-controlled' uses the settings supplied by the game. 'Manual' allows to override those values with the settings below.

items.label: (GPU) Manual position X
items.info: X offset of the frame buffer. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

items.label: (GPU) Manual position Y
items.info: Y offset of the frame buffer. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

items.label: (GPU) Manual height adjustment
items.info: Height adjustment. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

sections.label: GPU Plugin
sections.info: Configure low-level settings of the NEON GPU plugin.

items.label: (GPU) Show Interlaced Video
items.info: When enabled, games that run in high resolution video modes (480i, 512i) will produced interlaced video output. While this displays correctly on CRT televisions, it will produce artifacts on modern displays. When disabled, all video is output in progressive format. Note: there are games that will glitch is this is off.

items.label: (GPU) Enhanced Resolution
items.info: Render games that do not already run in high resolution video modes (480i, 512i) at twice the native internal resolution. Improves the fidelity of 3D models at the expense of increased performance requirements. 2D elements are generally unaffected by this setting.

items.label: (GPU) Enhanced Resolution Speed Hack
items.info: ('Enhanced Resolution' Hack) Improves performance but reduces compatibility and may cause rendering errors.

items.label: (GPU) Enhanced Resolution Texture Adjustment
items.info: ('Enhanced Resolution' Hack) Solves some texturing issues in some games in Enhanced Resolution mode. May cause a small performance hit.

sections.label: Audio
sections.info: Configure sound emulation: reverb, interpolation, CD audio decoding.

items.label: Audio Reverb Effects
items.info: Enable emulation of the reverb feature provided by the PSX SPU. Can be disabled to improve performance at the expense of reduced audio quality/authenticity.

items.label: Sound Interpolation
items.info: Enable emulation of the in-built audio interpolation provided by the PSX SPU. 'Gaussian' sounds closest to original hardware. 'Simple' improves performance but reduces quality. 'Cubic' has the highest performance requirements but produces increased clarity. Can be disabled entirely for maximum performance, at the expense of greatly reduced audio quality.

items.label: CD Audio
items.info: Enable playback of CD (CD-DA) audio tracks. Can be disabled to improve performance in games that include CD audio, at the expense of missing music.

items.label: XA Decoding
items.info: Enable playback of XA (eXtended Architecture ADPCM) audio tracks. Can be disabled to improve performance in games that include XA audio, at the expense of missing music.

items.label: Threaded SPU
items.info: Emulates the PSX SPU on another CPU thread. May cause audio glitches in some games.

sections.label: Input
sections.info: Configure input devices: analog response, haptic feedback, Multitaps, light guns, etc.

items.label: Analog Axis Bounds
items.info: Specify range limits for the left and right analog sticks when input device is set to 'analog' or 'dualshock'. 'Square' bounds improve input response when using controllers with highly circular ranges that are unable to fully saturate the X and Y axes at 45 degree deflections.

items.label: Rumble Effects
items.info: Enable haptic feedback when using a rumble-equipped gamepad with input device set to 'dualshock'.

items.label: DualShock Analog Mode Toggle Key Combo
items.info: When the input device type is DualShock, this option allows the emulated DualShock to be toggled between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode like original hardware. You can select the button combination for this.

items.label: Multitap Mode
items.info: Connect a virtual PSX Multitap peripheral to either controller 'Port 1' or controller 'Port 2' for 5 player simultaneous input, or to both 'Ports 1 and 2' for 8 player input. Mutlitap usage requires compatible games.

items.label: NegCon Twist Deadzone
items.info: Set the deadzone of the RetroPad left analog stick when simulating the 'twist' action of emulated neGcon Controllers. Used to eliminate drift/unwanted input.

items.label: NegCon Twist Response
items.info: Specify the analog response when using a RetroPad left analog stick to simulate the 'twist' action of emulated neGcon Controllers.

items.label: Mouse Sensitivity
items.info: Adjust responsiveness of emulated 'mouse' input devices.

items.label: Player 1 Lightgun Crosshair
items.info: Toggle player 1's crosshair for the Guncon or Konami Gun. Only works if RGB32 output is off (video options).

items.label: Player 2 Lightgun Crosshair
items.info: Toggle player 2's crosshair for the Guncon or Konami Gun. Only works if RGB32 output is off (video options).

items.label: Konami Gun X Axis Offset
items.info: Apply an X axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Konami Gun (Hyper Blaster / Justifier) device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

items.label: Konami Gun Y Axis Offset
items.info: Apply a Y axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Konami Gun (Hyper Blaster / Justifier) device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

items.label: Guncon X Axis Offset
items.info: Apply an X axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

items.label: Guncon Y Axis Offset
items.info: Apply a Y axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

items.label: Guncon X Axis Response
items.info: Adjust relative magnitude of horizontal light gun motion when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

items.label: Guncon Y Axis Response
items.info: Adjust relative magnitude of vertical light gun motion when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

sections.label: Compatibility Fixes
sections.info: Configure settings/workarounds required for correct operation of specific games.

items.label: Instruction Cache Emulation
items.info: Enable emulation of the PSX CPU instruction cache. Improves accuracy at the expense of increased performance overheads. Required for Formula One 2001, Formula One Arcade and Formula One 99. [Interpreter only; partial on lightrec and ARM dynarecs]

items.label: Exception and Breakpoint Emulation
items.info: Enable emulation of some almost never used PSX's debug features. This causes a performance hit, is not useful for games and is intended for PSX homebrew and romhack developers only. Only enable if you know what you are doing. [Interpreter only]

items.label: Disable Automatic Compatibility Hacks
items.info: By default, PCSX-ReARMed will apply auxiliary compatibility hacks automatically, based on the currently loaded content. This behaviour is required for correct operation, but may be disabled if desired.

sections.label: Speed Hacks (Advanced)
sections.info: Configure hacks that may improve performance at the expense of decreased accuracy/stability.

items.label: Turbo CD
items.info: This makes the emulated CD-ROM extremely fast and can reduce loading times in some cases. Warning: many games were not programmed to handle such a speed. The game (or even the emulator) MAY CRASH at ANY TIME if this is enabled.

items.label: (Speed Hack) Disable SMC Checks
items.info: Will cause crashes when loading, and lead to memory card failure.

items.label: (Speed Hack) Assume GTE Registers Unneeded
items.info: May cause rendering errors.

items.label: (Speed Hack) Disable GTE Flags
items.info: Will cause rendering errors.

items.label: Disable CPU/GTE Stalls
items.info: Will cause some games to run too quickly. Should be disabled in almost all cases.
